task: Cycle 2 robust thermoelectric PF-ZT frontier and measurement-design gate
evidence_convention: Source-reported literature, internally reconstructed model results, finite computations, and nature-level evidence are distinguished. No nature-level profile or material result was acquired.

claims.exact_statement: For fixed-sign branch B>0, let A,B,C,a lie in the literal box [A_lo,A_hi] x [B_lo,B_hi] x [C_lo,C_hi] x [a_lo,a_hi], with A_lo>0, a_lo>0, B_lo>0, and denominator positive throughout. For PF=B^2/A and ZT=B^2/[A(C+a)-B^2], the exact infima over the box are PF_lower=B_lo^2/A_hi and ZT_lower=B_lo^2/[A_hi(C_hi+a_hi)-B_lo^2]. If the uncertainty radii are profile-independent, the supremum of ZT_lower subject to PF_lower>=p0 over measurable 0<=phi<=1 equals the supremum over saturated energy intervals, including limiting half-lines. The same interval reduction holds when radii depend on center moments A,B only.
assumptions: Single-temperature near-equilibrium Boltzmann/RTA moment model with w(x)=1/[4 cosh(x/2)^2].
Uniform pointwise cap Sigma_max is supplied and the normalized transport profile is measurable with 0<=phi<=1.
The normalized lattice leak a is positive and independent of changes to phi; its uncertainty is represented by the supplied interval.
The B uncertainty interval stays on one sign branch; reflection x->-x handles the opposite sign.
The rectangular moment/leak set is the stated adversarial set. It can conservatively include physically infeasible combinations because A,B,C share one spectrum.
The uncertainty radii do not vary with profile beyond possible dependence on A,B.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/materials_energy/thermoelectric/CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Interface and exact robust certificate'; base equal-moment rearrangement is reconstructed in work/agents/materials_energy/thermoelectric/FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Conditional Pareto theorem'.
claims.novelty_boundary: The corner evaluation is generic monotonicity and the interval shape is already central in bounded-transport and Landauer thermoelectric optimization. Ding's article text directly reports a boxcar optimal transmission for arbitrary density-of-modes bounds M(x) and lattice conductance parameter beta. The present robust PF-floor equality is an equal-moment/rearrangement extension; no priority claim is made. Supplementary source proofs were not fully reconstructed in this cycle.
costs: Acquire a simultaneous uncertainty region for A, B, C, and lattice leakage a, including covariance and calibration/systematic floors.
Measure or infer energy-resolved transport and the supplied transport cap; charge temperature control, energy resolution, sample preparation, and computation.
Measure kappa_l independently or report uncertainty induced by subtracting kappa_e from total kappa; charge every device heat path, including contacts, radiation, and parasitic conduction.
Charge feature resolution, filter fabrication, yield, interface resistance, profile drift, gates/control work, and any change in lattice conduction.
The finite endpoint search scales quadratically in number of energy-grid bins after cumulative moments are tabulated; the theorem itself does not require that discretization.
claims.falsifier: A verified tuple in the stated rectangular set with positive denominator whose PF or ZT falls below the displayed corner value falsifies the corner formula. A noninterval profile with the same A,B and the same profile-independent uncertainty bounds but greater worst-case ZT falsifies the interval reduction. If measurement radii depend on profile, the claim does not apply.
claims.next_gate: Acquire a named sample/device, energy-resolved transport distribution and cap, joint A/B/C covariance or confidence set, and an independent interval for kappa_l; then compare matched-A,B interval-filter and noninterval profiles including all contact and parasitic channels.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed candidate with center moments A,B,C,a and deterministic moment/leak radii e_A,e_B,e_C,e_a on the positive-B branch, robust PF>=p0 and robust ZT>=z0 are equivalent to (B-e_B)^2>=p0(A+e_A) and (1+z0)(B-e_B)^2>=z0(A+e_A)(C+a+e_C+e_a), assuming positive robust denominator. Under e_i=q_i s_i/sqrt(n_i) with specified simultaneous-coverage multipliers q_i and noise scales s_i, minimizing acquisition energy sum_i u_i n_i over positive integer n_i subject to these inequalities is the exact conditional discrete measurement-allocation problem. In the small-error regime with PF slack, the continuous local relaxation with target-margin budget sum_i g_i e_i<=tau and cost sum_i alpha_i/e_i^2 has interior optimum e_i=tau*(alpha_i/g_i)^(1/3)/sum_j alpha_j^(1/3)g_j^(2/3), with minimum local cost [sum_j alpha_j^(1/3)g_j^(2/3)]^3/tau^2 and g=(z0(C+a),2(1+z0)B,z0 A,z0 A).
assumptions: Measurement intervals jointly cover the true parameter tuple at the stated confidence level; q_i are selected by an explicitly valid joint procedure or multiplicity adjustment.
Independent repeat model e_i=q_i s_i/sqrt(n_i) is appropriate over the sample and temperature range.
The closed-form allocation is a first-order local approximation, PF remains slack, and the optimum lies in the interior without systematic error floors or precision caps.
Acquisition energy per repeat u_i and the local cost coefficient alpha_i are supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: Threshold algebra and local Lagrange allocation are generic robust-estimation/design mathematics, not a new thermoelectric measurement principle. The cited studies support the importance and real cost of uncertainty characterization, not the proposed noise law for a specific sample.
costs: Instrument and sample energy/time per acquisition, calibration, repeated specimens, joint confidence construction, and computational effort.
Systematic bias floors and drift prevent arbitrarily tight intervals and must be estimated independently.
Filter/gate/control operating work and fabrication energy are outside the local statistical allocation unless added to its cost function.
claims.falsifier: For supplied q_i,s_i,u_i and a declared simultaneous-coverage/error model, any allocation whose true covered parameters violate the claimed robust PF or ZT threshold falsifies the certificate implementation or coverage assumptions. A lower-cost integer allocation than a separately certified global optimum would falsify that optimizer; no global numerical optimizer is claimed here.
claims.next_gate: Measure the joint covariance and bias floor for the four channels on an actual material/device, then solve and verify the exact nonlinear allocation program against equal-total-energy allocation and the laboratory's existing standard protocol.

claims.exact_statement: There is no universal measurement-channel allocation or robust material-design policy derivable from the current task record: neither the joint uncertainty set, the confidence level, nor the precision-versus-time/energy/fabrication costs of A, B, C, and a were supplied. Two admissible positive cost vectors with opposite relative channel costs can reverse which channel receives the marginal measurement effort, so a data-independent ranking is not identifiable.
assumptions: The permitted measurement channels enter at least one active robust margin with positive sensitivity.
No acquisition noise/cost model beyond the generic task interface has been supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a nonidentifiability result about the missing inputs, not a claim that optimal measurement design is impossible once those inputs are measured.
costs: Any actionable policy must charge parameter estimation, confidence, systematic error, instrument energy, specimen acquisition, filter fabrication, and device operating work.
Realization of an ideal boxcar may change lattice conductivity and complete-device heat paths; these couplings are not represented by fixed a.
claims.falsifier: A supplied named material with validated joint uncertainty and cost functions would remove the missing-input premise and permit a numerical policy; it would not make a universal policy possible across arbitrary cost models.
claims.next_gate: Request no further abstract optimization. Resume with acquired material/device uncertainty and cost curves, and compare against a same-data center-ZT baseline subject to the same robust PF floor.

finite_computation.status: finite-grid illustration only; not a theorem verification, measurement, or material prediction
finite_computation.method: Enumerated saturated intervals on x in [-1,15] at step 0.02 using cycle-1 cumulative Fermi-window moments. Used center a=0.1; absolute radii e_A=0.01,e_B=0.01,e_C=0.02,e_a=0.02; compared center-ZT and worst-box-ZT objectives subject to the same worst-box normalized PF floor 1.0.
finite_computation.result: Center-ZT objective under robust PF floor chooses [1.76,6.30] with center ZT 5.1130242 and worst-box ZT 2.6056070. Worst-box objective chooses [1.46,5.18] with center ZT 4.8517173 and worst-box ZT 2.6984216. The latter raises the grid worst-case value about 3.6% and lowers center ZT about 5.1%. The radii are hypothetical and no confidence level is assigned.
